text:
Yes — Monzo is a real, fully regulated UK bank. Although it started out in 2015 as a prepaid card and spending app, it received its full UK banking licence in April 2017.   
Monzo
+ 1

Monzo holds the same regulatory status and protections as traditional high street banks like Barclays, Lloyds, or HSBC:

Full Regulation: Monzo Bank Limited is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) and regulated by both the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and the PRA (Firm Reference Number: 730427).

Is Monzo Safe in 2026? FSCS, Fraud & Security Explained
“Monzo Bank Limited is regulated by the FCA and PRA and authorised by the PRA. Its Financial Services Register number is 730427. Can I Safely Have My Salary Paid...”

FSCS Protection: Eligible deposits held with Monzo are protected by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) up to £120,000 per person (£240,000 for joint accounts). Because Monzo holds its own standalone banking licence and does not share it with another brand, you get the full £120,000 protection limit independently of any other banks you use. (Note: This differs from some fintech competitors like Wise or Revolut's standard UK e-money accounts, which use "safeguarding" rather than direct FSCS bank deposit protection.)   
UK Finance Blog
+ 2

Full Banking Features: You get a standard UK sort code and 8-digit account number, Direct Debits, standing orders, BACS/Faster Payments, and access to traditional credit products like arranged overdrafts, personal loans, and credit-like instalment features (Monzo Flex).   
Digital Bank Networks

The main practical difference between Monzo and a traditional bank is simply that Monzo is digital-first and has no physical branches. Everything—including customer support—is managed through the app (or a basic emergency web portal), and if you ever need to deposit physical cash, you do so at a PayPoint or Post Office for a small fee (or free within monthly allowances on certain paid plans).
